newsitem.title: USA: Insurers must decide on Calif. agency by Nov. 8.
newsitem.headline: Insurers must decide on Calif. agency by Nov. 8.

text.p: The California Earthquake Authority must win the backing of at least 70 percent of the California residential insurance market by November 8 for the agency to become operational.
The California insurance department said it has received verbal assurances from all the major insurance companies, but has not yet received official commitments.
"We're not too concerned about that," California insurance department spokesman Richard Wiebe said.
He said the department did not foresee any problems getting the required industry backing for the authority, which would issue no-frills earthquake insurance policies to California homeowners.
However, without the required 70 percent industry backing, the earthquake authority would be, at the very least, delayed for a long time, Wiebe said.
With the participation of 70 percent of the market, the insurance industry would contribute an initial $700 million to fund the earthquake authority.
The industry would be obligated to make additional capital commitments to pay claims if an earthquake strikes.
The earthquake authority also plans to purchase about $1.4 billion in reinsurance and will have a $1 billion line of credit arranged by Chase Manhattan.
An offering of catastrophe-linked bonds, led by Morgan Stanley and co-managed by Bear Stearns and Goldman Sachs, is expected to raise another $1 billion or so.
Meanwhile, Allstate Corp on Thursday said it plans to resume normal business operations in the California homeowners market as of November 4 because of the creation of the earthquake authority.
"We're confident and hopeful that we'll have full participation" in the earthquake authority, an Allstate spokesman said.
But Safeco Corp chief financial officer Rod Pierson, speaking to Reuters on Monday, said the company was still undecided about whether or not to participate in the earthquake authority.
Pierson said it was not clear if participation in the authority would reduce the company's earthquake exposure enough to make it worthwhile.
And Safeco can managed its exposures through reinsurance, unlike some of the larger personal lines companies like Allstate, he added.
